historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.8-3.3%) diverges sharply from reported EPS CAGR (36-58%): reported EPS is dominated by exceptional gains (Airtel/Intouch/Comcentre sales) and the FY21 impairment trough. Underlying NPAT CAGR is ~10% (FY21 1,733 -> FY26 2,769), driven mostly by associates. Revenue has declined since FY16 (divestments of Amobee/Trustwave, AUD weakness). The OpCo forward path (2-3%) is anchored to guidance, not to any of these CAGRs.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (no equity-award taxes; interest income excluded only when net cash, which Singtel does not hold). SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs are near-identical because SBC is ~S$32-43m/yr. Group FCF includes associate dividends (S$1.25-1.39bn/yr) so its CAGR is not an OpCo growth measure.

scenario_narratives.base: OpCos grow in line with the cautious FY27 guide (EBIT +low-to-mid single digits) then 2.5-3%: NCS converts its record S$3.8bn bookings, Nxera's DC Tuas and GPU-as-a-Service fill, Optus holds price rises and network-sharing revenue while absorbing Triple Zero remediation, and Singapore mobile keeps eroding at the margin. Elevated FY27 growth capex (S$1.2bn, S$0.7bn partner-funded) fades to a core ~15% of revenue. Associates are taken at today's market value less a 15% haircut; capital recycling (S$5.8bn of S$9bn done) converts stakes to cash at roughly that value, so it neither adds nor destroys value here.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Singtel28 turnaround works: Optus EBIT keeps compounding as in FY26 (+23%) with no further outage, data centres and RE:AI become a meaningful high-margin growth leg (combined ~2.8GW platform via STT GDC), NCS AI work lifts margins, and EBITDA margin reaches 30.5%. Revenue grows 4-4.5% for three years. Upside in the associates (Airtel's Indian tariff cycle, AIS) is not in this scenario because the bridge is held at market across scenarios.
scenario_narratives.bear: Optus suffers another major failure or a punitive regulatory outcome (ACMA/ACCC fines, licence conditions, lost enterprise/government contracts) and its turnaround stalls; Singapore's four-player price war and travel eSIMs keep shrinking Singtel Singapore EBITDA (-6.8% FY26); AI/data-centre capex earns below its cost as capacity floods the region. Revenue grows ~1-1.5%, EBITDA margin drifts to 25.5%, and capex stays near 15% of revenue. Associate downside (INR/IDR/THB depreciation, Airtel AGR dues, XLSmart pressure on Telkomsel) is NOT modelled here because the bridge is common to all scenarios; see key risks.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Singtel is a holding of listed emerging-market telcos wrapped around a mature, capital-hungry developed-market OpCo. Most of the value (~S$3.2/share net of the haircut, perpetuals and NCI) is the associate/investment portfolio, which is taken at market value rather than re-forecast, so the scenarios move only the OpCo (~S$0.6-0.9/share). The OpCo is valued on owner FCF after leases, spectrum and the Singtel-funded share of data-centre capex, which is far below reported group FCF because reported FCF includes S$1.25bn of associate dividends and excludes lease and spectrum payments. The 15% haircut on listed stakes is the largest single judgment: removing it adds S$0.53/share.
key_risks_to_valuation: Associate market values: each 10% move in Airtel alone is ~S$0.22/share (after haircut); the bridge is common to all three scenarios, so the bear/bull spread understates total risk.
EM FX: INR, IDR, THB and PHP depreciation against SGD translates directly into the bridge and into associate dividends.
Optus operational/regulatory events (outages, ACMA/ACCC penalties, remediation provisions S$266m FY26).
Data-centre/AI capex (S$1.2bn growth capex FY27; STT GDC 25% stake on completion) earning below cost of capital.
Telkomsel is unlisted and valued at ~8x share of profit; TLKM.JK has fallen 27% since March and XLSmart competition is intensifying.

Singtel's own share price fell from S$4.94 (31 Mar 2026) to S$4.12 while its listed stakes were broadly flat in SGD; the H1 FY2027 result (due Nov 2026) has not been extracted and may contain the explanation.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 3.99-5.27. Associate prices and FX from the same API, 2026-10-22/23 closes vs 2026-03-30/31.
data_sources.financials: Z74.SI_Metrics.csv; FY2026 results/financial statements (Z74.SI_Annual_FY2026-FinancialStatements.txt), FY2026 MDA (capex guidance, Optus/Group cash flow), FY2026 Annual Report notes 24-25 (associate/JV market values, dividends) and note 30 (lease liabilities).
data_sources.qualitative: Z74.SI_Analysis.json (2026-10-24): guidance, Singtel28 plan, Optus incidents, capital recycling.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report statement of changes in equity, 'Equity-settled share-based payment' S$43.3m (Z74.SI_Annual_FY2026.txt:8884). No net-share-settlement tax line; awards are delivered from shares bought in the market ('Purchase of performance shares' S$157.1m FY26, financing).
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted average for H2 FY2026 (16,549.1m; FY2026 results note 11). Held FLAT: SBC (0.3% of revenue) is expensed in the flows. The up-to-S$2.0bn value-realisation buyback (S$103.9m done in FY26) is funded from asset-recycling proceeds and is value-neutral at fair value, so it is not modelled as share shrinkage.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T09:06:02Z regular close (SGX), Yahoo Finance chart API
inputs.wacc_rationale: WACC 7.0% in SGD/AUD terms for the consolidated OpCos (Singtel Singapore, Optus, NCS, Digital InfraCo; ~50% of revenue Australian). Blended risk-free ~3.3% (10y SGS ~2.4%, 10y ACGB ~4.3%, weighted to OpCo revenue), ERP 5.5%, beta 0.8 -> cost of equity ~7.7%; after-tax cost of debt ~2.9% (A1/A rated, ~87% fixed), ~20-25% debt weight -> ~6.8-7.0%, rounded to 7.0%. Same rate in all three scenarios: Optus execution/regulatory risk is charged in the scenario weights (bear 25%), not as a WACC premium (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. lease_cost_pct_path 4.1% = FY26 lease payments S$444.0m (financing) + interest on lease liabilities S$142.8m (finance costs note 8) = S$586.8m on S$14,260.6m revenue. D&A path is EX right-of-use depreciation (FY26 total D&A 2,343.9 less ROU depreciation 417.0 = 1,926.9, 13.5% of revenue). Lease liabilities (S$3,146.9m: 405.0 current + 2,741.9 non-current, note 30) are EXCLUDED from net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; NCI (S$157.3m at book, 31 Mar 2026, mainly data-centre capital partners) deducted once in the equity bridge. NCI share of profit is only S$11.2m FY26. Note FY27 growth capex of S$1.2bn is S$0.7bn externally funded (capital partners + customer advances); the capex path below carries only the Singtel-funded share, so partner-funded assets are matched by their NCI claim rather than charged to Singtel.
inputs.net_debt_note: Singtel-defined net debt S$8,728m at 31 Mar 2026 (gross debt incl. lease liabilities, adjusted for hedging balances, less cash and fixed deposits incl. >3 months; FY26 MDA p.622) less lease liabilities S$3,146.9m = S$5,581.1m net financial debt. total_debt 9,051.5 = 5,581.1 + cash 3,470.4 (i.e. borrowings ex-leases S$8,531.8m plus ~S$520m of net hedging liability net of >3-month deposits).
inputs.notes: MODEL: Sum-of-parts per dcf-methods SKILL.md ('value the parts separately and sum') using the owner-FCF engine plus owner-fcf-adaptations (d) matching-asset rule. Singtel is two businesses: (1) consolidated OpCos (Singtel Singapore, Optus, NCS, Digital InfraCo) valued by the component owner-FCF DCF, and (2) equity-accounted regional associates/JVs (Airtel 27.5%, Telkomsel 30.1%, AIS 24.8%, Globe 46.6% economic) plus FVOCI stakes (Gulf Development 7.7%), whose share of profit (S$1,945m FY26) is more than the OpCos earn. A single-stream DCF of group FCF would be wrong both ways: reported FCF (S$2,439m) contains S$1,249m of associate dividends (a small fraction of their earnings, since Airtel reinvests) and excludes spectrum and lease payments. So associate dividends and their withholding tax are STRIPPED from the flows and the stakes enter the equity_bridge at market value marked to 23 Oct 2026, with a 15% realisation/holdco haircut on listed stakes. FY0 owner FCF on the engine's OpCo-only basis is roughly S$0.4-0.5bn (EBITDA 3,848 - leases 587 - SBC 43 - tax ~207 - capex 2,482 - intangibles/spectrum 121 + WC 163); last_fcf (2,395.4 = reported FCF - SBC) is the group figure for audit only and is NOT the engine's base, which is built from components. The FY2026 S$2.84bn net exceptional gain (mainly partial Airtel sales) is excluded: it is a conversion of bridge asset into cash, not operating flow. Buybacks: Singtel is a repurchaser (S$103.9m cancelled + S$157.1m performance-share purchases FY26), so the flat count is funded. SBC is small (0.3% of revenue); house and street bases nearly coincide.
inputs.associates_note: Group's share of market value at 31 Mar 2026 from FY2026 AR note 24 (Z74.SI_Annual_FY2026.txt:12406): Airtel S$40,993.1m, Globe S$2,326.2m, AIS S$10,776.3m; quoted associates S$1.13bn (note 25); Gulf FVOCI quoted S$2,685.9m (FY26 results note 12). Marked to 2026-10-23 via Yahoo: BHARTIARTL.NS 1782.4 -> 1892.1 INR and SGDINR 72.724 -> 74.277 (x1.0393); ADVANC.BK 373 -> 336 THB and SGDTHB 25.301 -> 26.412 (x0.8630); Globe via ADR GTMEY 23.12 -> 27.68 USD and USDSGD 1.2843 -> 1.2779 (x1.1912; GLO.PS not served by Yahoo, ADR is thin OTC); GULF.BK 59.25 -> 61.75 THB (x0.9984). Quoted associates (SingPost etc.) held at 31-Mar value.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 guidance: OpCo EBIT +low-to-mid single digits (cautious, Middle East/energy). Revenue +2.5% FY27 (NCS bookings S$3.8bn record, Nxera DC Tuas ramp, Optus price rises) easing to 2% by year 8.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY26 EBITDA 27.0% (pre-IFRS16 lease cost). 27.1% in FY27 reproduces ~4% OpCo EBIT growth on guidance; +0.3pp/yr to 28.5% as higher-margin data centres and S$0.2bn/yr cost savings mix in, offset by Singapore mobile price competition.
base.capex_rationale: FY27 guided total capex ~S$3.0bn of which S$0.7bn externally funded -> Singtel-funded ~S$2.3bn (15.7%) + ~1.5% for spectrum/other intangibles (FY23-26 average S$566m incl. Optus FY25 renewal S$1.7bn) = 17.2%. Fades to core S$1.8bn-equivalent (12.6%) + spectrum 1.5% + DC maintenance ~1% = 15% steady state, slightly above D&A ex-ROU (14.5%).
base.cash_tax_rationale: FY26 tax paid on operating activities S$207m (ex withholding tax on associate dividends, which is stripped with those dividends) on engine-basis EBIT ~S$1.29bn = 16%. Ramps to 20% (Singapore 17%, Australia 30%, Pillar Two 15% floor) as Optus taxable profit rebuilds.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because Optus carries single-regulator, politically charged risk (two serious outages in three years, fatalities linked to the 2025 Triple Zero failure, CFO/CIO departures) and management has itself cut the FY27 growth outlook. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (Optus execution, AI/data-centre returns, NCS margins). Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
